name: Nyons
summary: Sun-trap olive town on the Eygues with a superb Provençal market and the medieval Rue des Grands Forts.
tip: Come Thursday for the market; oil mills sell direct year-round.

name: Vaison-la-Romaine
summary: Two towns in one: extensive Roman ruins and a Roman bridge below, a cobbled medieval Haute Ville above.
tip: Combine ruins in the morning with the Haute Ville and lunch.

name: Buis-les-Baronnies
summary: Lime-blossom capital tucked under the Rocher Saint-Julien, with arcaded squares and great climbing.
tip: The Saint-Julien cliffs above town are a classic climbing spot.

name: Grignan
summary: Renaissance château on a rock, immortalised by Madame de Sévigné, ringed by lavender in summer.
tip: Lavender peaks late June to mid-July around the château.

name: Montbrun-les-Bains
summary: One of France’s "plus beaux villages", stacked up a hillside facing Mont Ventoux, with a thermal spa.
tip: Book the thermal baths ahead if you want a spa afternoon.

name: Séguret
summary: A "plus beau village" clinging to the Dentelles, with a covered lane, fountain and sweeping vineyard views.
tip: Tiny lanes — park below and walk up.

name: Dieulefit
summary: Pottery town in a mild micro-climate, full of ceramic studios and a lively Friday market.
tip: Detour to the perched Templar village of Le Poët-Laval.

name: Die
summary: Gateway to the Diois and the Vercors, a Roman-walled town famous for its sparkling Clairette.
tip: Pair the town with a Clairette tasting or a Vercors drive.

name: Orange
summary: Home to the best-preserved Roman theatre in Europe and a triumphal arch, both UNESCO listed.
tip: The Chorégies opera festival fills the Roman theatre in summer.

name: Nyons olive mills
summary: Taste AOC Nyons olive oil and black olives straight from the mill — Vignolis co-op and the historic Autrand-Dozol mill.
tip: Olive harvest & new oil run roughly December–January.

name: Vinsobres & Côtes du Rhône
summary: Cru village of the southern Rhône — cellar-door tastings across Vinsobres, Rasteau and Cairanne.
tip: Most caveaux welcome walk-ins; midweek is quietest.

name: Gigondas & the Dentelles wine road
summary: Prestige reds beneath the Dentelles de Montmirail, with tasting rooms in Gigondas, Vacqueyras and Beaumes-de-Venise.
tip: The village caveau pours dozens of estates in one stop.

name: Clairette de Die cellars
summary: Sparkling Clairette made by the ancestral method — visit the Jaillance cave in Die for a tour and tasting.
tip: Free self-guided tour + tasting at the co-op.

name: Richerenches truffle market
summary: The Rhône’s black-truffle capital — a famous winter Saturday market in a Templar-walled village.
tip: Season only — mid-November to mid-March, Saturday mornings.

name: Montélimar nougat
summary: The nougat capital, with historic makers you can tour, plus a lively old town and Saturday market.
tip: Several nougateries offer free tastings and workshop tours.

name: Rémuzat vulture cliffs
summary: Griffon vultures wheel over the Rocher du Caire — one of the best raptor-watching spots in France.
tip: Late morning thermals give the best soaring; bring binoculars.

name: Gorges du Toulourenc
summary: A walk *in* the river below Mont Ventoux — wade the shallow gorge between limestone walls on a hot day.
tip: Summer only; wear water shoes and check the flow after rain.

name: Dentelles de Montmirail
summary: Serrated limestone ridges rising out of the vineyards — walking, scrambling and world-class rock climbing.
tip: Park at Col du Cayron for the classic ridge loop.

name: Mont Ventoux summit road
summary: Drive (or cycle) to the 1,909 m "Giant of Provence" for a lunar summit and vast Alpine-to-sea views.
tip: Summit road usually closed by snow roughly Nov–Apr; it’s cold up top — bring a layer.

name: Forêt de Saoû
summary: A hidden syncline forest ringed by cliffs — shady picnic meadows, easy trails and the Trois Becs skyline.
tip: Great shady option on scorching days; ideal for an easy family walk.

name: Avignon
summary: City of the Popes — the vast Gothic Palais des Papes, the half-bridge of the song, and a buzzing walled centre.
tip: Go early in July or you’ll share it with the whole festival.

name: Pont du Gard
summary: The colossal three-tier Roman aqueduct over the Gardon — a UNESCO icon you can swim beneath in summer.
tip: Bring swimwear — the pebble beach under the arches is the highlight in summer.

name: Gorges de l’Ardèche & Pont d’Arc
summary: A canyon carved by the Ardèche with the natural Pont d’Arc bridge — kayaking, swimming and clifftop belvederes.
tip: Kayak the gorge in summer, or just drive the belvedere road for the views.

name: Gorges du Verdon
summary: Europe’s grandest canyon — turquoise water, vertiginous rim roads and the Lac de Sainte-Croix.
tip: A full day — go for the drama when you want something bigger than the Baronnies.

name: Plateau de Valensole (lavender)
summary: Endless lavender rows to the horizon — the postcard of Provence, at its peak in early July.
tip: Strictly seasonal — bloom is roughly the first three weeks of July.

name: Les Baux-de-Provence & Alpilles
summary: A dramatic clifftop citadel in the Alpilles, plus the immersive Carrières des Lumières light show.
tip: Pair the fortress with the projected-art quarry next door.

name: L’Isle-sur-la-Sorgue
summary: The "Venice of Provence" — canals, waterwheels and the antiques capital of the south, with permanent dealer villages and a famous Sunday brocante.
tip: Sunday is the big brocante day; dealer villages also open Sat–Mon.

name: Lyon
summary: France’s gastronomic capital — Renaissance Vieux Lyon, traboules, bouchons and the Fourvière hill.
tip: Book a bouchon for lunch; the city rewards a full day or an overnight.

name: Grenoble & the Vercors
summary: Alpine city ringed by peaks — ride the Bastille bubble-cars, then escape into the Vercors plateau.
tip: The Bastille cable-car gives instant mountain views over the city.
